issues.issue: The parenthetical defining the parties is garbled (“Managers Fund and Manager each being referred to mdividually as a ‘Borrower’”), so the label attached to B-4 Partners is not cleanly stated. The joint-and-several designation is otherwise plain.

“Control” is defined only as “the power to direct the management and policies of a Person,” and the 10%-ownership deeming rules are expressly confined to the Eligible Notes Receivable definition and Section 7.13, inviting an expressio unius argument about affiliation elsewhere. Whether a 10% holder is an “Affiliate” for any other purpose is left open.

The definition ends with an open-ended catch-all, “together with any obligations undertaken or assumed relating thereto,” appended to two specific enumerated obligations, leaving the reach of “relating thereto” uncertain. Because Approved Debt is both permitted Indebtedness and secured by Permitted Liens, the boundary matters.

Lender's approval of new title companies “will not be unreasonably withheld”, yet Lender may remove any company “in its reasonable discretion” — two different standards inside one definition. Which controls a contested removal is not stated.

Clause (c) permits “an informal or unwritten estimate of value by Servicer” to count as an “Authorized Appraisal,” which sits against clause (a)'s FIRREA-compliant standard and largely swallows it. Which alternative governs a given valuation is not fixed.

“Any financial accommodation extended … by a Bank Product Provider” is a broad general phrase followed by a seven-item “including” list, so the outer reach of “financial accommodation” is undefined. Because Bank Product Obligations are secured by the Collateral, the scope has consequences.

The Bank Product Reserve is deducted from the Borrowing Base at Lender's election, while Section 2.1(b) states that Lender “agrees not to establish any such reserves unless a Triggering Event has occurred”; whether that limit reaches this reserve is arguable.

“A reference in this Agreement to a Borrower shall be a reference to each of and either of Fund and Manager” is internally muddled: “each of” and “either of” point to different readings of every singular use of “Borrower.” Whether an obligation binds both entities or only one turns on this phrase.

The grant covers “all property, including, without limitation” twelve enumerated categories, so the enumerated list may either illustrate or limit the general words. Clause (k) — “money or other assets … that come into the possession, custody, or control of the Lender” — is especially open-ended.

The definition incorporates an unattached extrinsic document (“in the form delivered to Lender and approved by Lender prior to the Closing Date”), so its content cannot be determined from the instrument. Amendments require Lender approval “in Lender's sole discretion,” compounding the indeterminacy.

“All cash, checks, notes, instruments, and other items of payment” is an unbounded definition with no possessive limiting it to a Borrower's receipts, and “other items of payment” is a catch-all after specifics. Its reach matters because Section 2.6 requires all Collections to be deposited to a Cash Management Account.

“Any Note Receivable that Administrative Borrower or Lender deems to be non-performing or non-collectible” makes status turn on either party's unilateral, undefined opinion, with no standard of reasonableness. “Non-performing” and “non-collectible” are themselves undefined.
